Issued at 330 AM CDT Mon Jul 20 2026

Current Conditions & Synoptic Overview:

Ridging aloft spanned the western 2/3 of the CONUS and well 
into central Canada in previous days, but this ridge is 
beginning to be flattened by a shortwave trough pushing across 
the Canadian Prairie. 00Z upper air analysis indicates that a 
zonal upper-level jet is developing across the Northern Rockies
and into the Northern Plains, cutting into the northern extent
of the ridge, and the 00Z sounding from Glasgow, Montana has 
already observed 100+kts within this strengthening jet streak. 
A surface low has developed in Manitoba in conjunction with this
upper-level disturbance, with a cold front extending south from
the low into central South Dakota. Weak surface high pressure 
sits over the Great Lakes on the other side of a stationary 
front, which is spread from Sioux City, IA to the southeast 
through Bethany, MO and towards St. Louis. Widespread visibility
reductions from wildfire smoke are apparent on regional 
observations in areas east of the front as the nocturnal 
boundary layer traps smoke near the surface.


Heat Today and Tuesday:

"Unpleasant" is not a strong enough word to describe today's
forecast conditions. As the ridge is flattened and pushed
eastward, low-level flow becomes more westerly, increasing 850mb
temperatures by 2-4C. High temperatures in the upper 90s and dew
points in the mid- to upper 70s will combine to create 
widespread heat indices of 105-110 degrees, likely with some 
localized spots in excess of 110 degrees. Soundings continue to
suggest that afternoon mixing should help to combat rising dew
points, but Sunday afternoon obs recorded upper 70s dew points
in some locations during peak mixing, and winds will be
similarly light today to Sunday, so the mixing that occurs will
likely not be strong enough to be effective at limiting dew
points very much. As such, Heat Advisory remains in place 
areawide from 1PM to 9PM this afternoon. Heat Risk guidance 
depicts widespread Major (Level 3 of 4) Heat Risk, suggesting
impacts to anyone without effective cooling or adequate 
hydration. Efforts should be made to stay indoors whenever
possible.

Little relief is expected during the overnight hours, with
tonight's low temperatures only dropping into the upper 70s and 
low 80s. As such, minimum heat indices will drop to upper 70s 
in much of the area, but the urban heat island in Kansas City 
will keep the minimum apparent temperature in the low 80s
overnight. The much-anticipated cold front looks to arrive so 
late Monday night that it's better described as Tuesday morning, 
with areas south of Interstate 70 unlikely to see frontal 
passage until after peak heating on Tuesday afternoon. For this
reason, kept the segment of the Heat Advisory that continues
until 7PM on Tuesday confined to these areas south of I-70,
where another day of 100-105+ degree heat indices are expected.


Storm Chances Late Tonight/Tuesday Morning:

Convection is expected to fire in Iowa late this afternoon into
this evening, initially as discrete cells and then forming into
multicell clusters. In the early hours of Tuesday morning, most
CAM guidance depicts storms becoming widespread and forming 
into a line along the front in north-central and northeast 
Missouri, with coverage becoming increasingly scattered/less 
organized along the front as you get further west. Depending 
where the prefrontal convection forms and develops to our north,
there is a scenario where we could see some storm leftovers 
move into the area ahead of the actual cold frontal passage, 
which would lead to multiple rounds of storms and an earlier 
precip onset time. However, this is the least likely potential 
scenario, with most CAM guidance depicting similar locations 
and timing windows for showers and storms, and primarily keeping
the most widespread storms to the east of most of our area.

As the upper-level jet streak begins to move into the Midwest
Monday night into Tuesday, shear profiles begin to improve, with
30-40kts of shear by 00Z Tuesday and continuing to increase
through the overnight hours. Instability will be best (3000J/kg+
MUCAPE) during the evening hours and along the front to our 
north, but wanes quickly after 1AM Tuesday, which is when the
window for the arrival of the front opens up. Due to the
unfavorable overlap of severe ingredients, the widespread 
severe weather risk for most of the area should be limited, but
we will have to monitor for potential severe winds with any 
clusters that develop to our north and move into the area 
overnight. Areas along and north of a Unionville to Kirksville
MO line are currently in an SPC Slight (Level 2 of 5) Risk for
severe storms, with a very narrow Marginal (Level 1 of 5) Risk
bracketing its southern edge.
